item.title: Dame Maria Kopkop calls on students to help build PNG’s future
item.description: Kopkop College Executive Director and Founder Dame Maria Kopkop has challenged the next generation of Papua New Guineans to use education, strong character, good health and responsible citizenship to help build the nation over the next 50 years. item.content:encoded:
Kopkop College Executive Director and Founder Dame Maria Kopkop has challenged the next generation of Papua New Guineans to use education, strong character, good health and responsible citizenship to help build the nation over the next 50 years.

Dame Maria made the call during Kopkop College’s 51st Independence anniversary celebrations in Port Moresby, where students, teachers, parents, school management and members of the community gathered to reflect on Papua New Guinea’s journey since independence and look towards the country’s future.

She said education must go beyond academic results and certificates.

She stressed that students must develop the knowledge, values and skills needed to contribute positively to society.

“Education is more than just passing examinations and receiving certificates. Education teaches you how to think, how to solve problems, how to make wise choices, how to respect others, and how to contribute to your country,” she said.

Dame Maria said the young generation would face new challenges as Papua New Guinea moves towards its centenary of independence in 2075.

“You will inherit challenges that my generation may not have completely solved, but you will inherit opportunities that earlier generations could never have imagined.

"Science and technology will continue to change the world, new careers will emerge, climate change will challenge our communities, and our health system will need drastic, important solutions.” Mama Kopkop said.

She said academic achievement must be supported by good character, honesty, discipline, compassion and courage.

“Our country will need honest leaders, skilled professionals, innovative thinkers, entrepreneurs, teachers, doctors, engineers, and importantly, responsible citizens. That is why I say to you today, children. Stand strong in your education. Knowledge without character cannot build a strong nation.”

Dame Maria also urged students to take responsibility for their physical and mental well-being.

“Look after your health. A strong mind needs a healthy body. Eat wisely, exercise, avoid harmful habits, care for your mental well-being, and build relationships that bring goodness into your life.” she added.

Looking towards 2075, Dame Maria said many of the students attending the celebration today would become the leaders, professionals, parents and grandparents of the future.

“In 2075, when Papua New Guinea celebrates 100 years of independence, many of you sitting here today will be the leaders, professionals, parents, and grandparents looking back on the journey.”

She expressed hope that the students would play an active role in building a peaceful, educated, healthy and prosperous Papua New Guinea.

“My hope, children, is that you will see a peaceful, educated, healthy, and prosperous nation, and that you will be able to say, ‘We helped build that."

Meanwhile the Director also encouraged students to understand and respect Papua New Guinea’s history, including the cultures, traditions, knowledge and communities that existed long before independence.

She said the country’s future development must continue to recognise the importance of culture, family values and the contribution of communities to nation-building.

Maria emphasised that Kopkop College’s education philosophy places emphasis on academic excellence, cultural values, family and the development of each child’s individual potential and this pillars will continue to remain.

item.title: Teachers warned of fake TSC officers on Facebook
item.description: The Teaching Service Commission [TSC] has warned teachers, especially recent graduates and those in very remote locations, not to be fooled by scammers operating on social media platforms like Facebook. TSC Acting Chairman Maini Mike Ugaia issued the warning following reports that fraudsters are tricking teachers into paying fake “legal service fees” to secure employment.
item.content:encoded:
The Teaching Service Commission [TSC] has warned teachers, especially recent graduates and those in very remote locations, not to be fooled by scammers operating on social media platforms like Facebook.

TSC Acting Chairman Maini Mike Ugaia issued the warning following reports that fraudsters are tricking teachers into paying fake “legal service fees” to secure employment.

Ugaia clarified that the Commission does not charge any fees for its services, stating that there is no such thing as a legal service fee or administrative charge within the TSC and the Education Department.

The Commission is aware of a fraudulent Facebook profile operating under the name Guina Robin, which has been falsely claiming to be a TSC officer and misleading teachers.

To prevent further exploitation, the TSC is advising all teachers to avoid conducting official business on social media.

Teachers are also reminded that Commission officers are stationed on the ground in every province.

Teachers with employment queries or paperwork issues are urged to visit their local provincial education office to speak with genuine staff face-to-face.

The public and the teaching fraternity are urged to remain vigilant and report any suspicious individuals or payment demands to the police or the TSC head office.

item.title: Districts told to direct 10% funding to SMEs
item.description: Prime Minister James Marape says 10% of funding allocated to each district in Papua New Guinea is intended to support Small and Medium Enterprises [SMEs], helping local businesses establish, grow and create opportunities for people in rural communities. He says every district in Papua New Guinea has different economic opportunities and needs.
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister James Marape says 10% of funding allocated to each district in Papua New Guinea is intended to support Small and Medium Enterprises [SMEs], helping local businesses establish, grow and create opportunities for people in rural communities.

He says every district in Papua New Guinea has different economic opportunities and needs.

Some districts have strong potential in tourism, while others are better suited to agriculture, forestry, fisheries and other industries.

The Prime Minister was speaking at Government House after the swearing-in of the two vice ministers last week.

The Government’s approach is aimed at making it easier for people in rural areas to access support and participate in economic activity by ensuring that districts allocate funding to assist local SMEs.

Prime Minister James Marape says people seeking assistance for their businesses should approach their respective Members of Parliament and district administrations, rather than travelling to the Prime Minister’s Office, City Governors or national government departments seeking business funding.

He emphasized that district members have a responsibility to ensure local communities benefit from available SME support.

Where such funding is not being provided, he said, people have the right to hold their elected representatives accountable.

Prime Minister James Marape says there should be no excuse for districts failing to support their people.

He said instructions have been given to district members to assist local SMEs, with particular emphasis on agriculture and tourism, as well as creating opportunities for young people.

item.title: TSC rejects claims of teacher’s pay rise
item.description: The Teaching Service Commission [TSC] Acting Chairman, Maini Mike Ugaia, has strongly disapproved recent media statements made by the Papua New Guinea Teachers Association [PNGTA] President regarding a premature teachers' pay increase. Chairman Ugaia clarified that while discussions and initial submissions concerning the 2026–2028 log of claims have been presented to the Department of Personnel Ma
item.content:encoded:
The Teaching Service Commission [TSC] Acting Chairman, Maini Mike Ugaia, has strongly disapproved recent media statements made by the Papua New Guinea Teachers Association [PNGTA] President regarding a premature teachers' pay increase.

Chairman Ugaia clarified that while discussions and initial submissions concerning the 2026–2028 log of claims have been presented to the Department of Personnel Management [DPM], any proposed salary adjustments between the TSC and the PNGTA remain strictly subject to DPM approval.

“The statement circulated in the media is untrue and misleading.

“The PNGTA President is advised to withdraw these unauthorized claims immediately. Negotiations are a formal administrative process, and creating false expectations among our hard-working teachers disrupts the stability of our education sector.” Acting Chairman Ugaia said.

He said releasing unverified public declarations regarding a pay increase is both premature and highly unprofessional.

Teachers throughout Papua New Guinea are urged not to rely on speculative media coverage or external announcements regarding their terms and conditions.

TSC remains the sole legal employer and authoritative body responsible for teacher welfare and salary matters; consequently, all teachers should obtain official updates directly from the TSC headquarters or through authorized TSC Media Announcements.

“The Commission extends its appreciation to our nearly 70,000 teachers nationwide for their unwavering commitment and dedication to our students throughout this academic year.

“As we enter the final term of the school calendar, we wish you all the very best and continued success in your classrooms.” Acting chairman Ugaia said.

item.title: CDF Cup 26 kicks off
item.description: The 2026 PNGDF Commanders Cup kicked off day one of matches today (Saturday 19th September) at the Murray Barracks Oval in Port Moresby. All ten units assembled at its Headquarters for the two weeks of competition.
item.content:encoded:
The 2026 PNGDF Commanders Cup kicked off day one of matches today (Saturday 19th September) at the Murray Barracks Oval in Port Moresby.

All ten units assembled at its Headquarters for the two weeks of competition.

Pool 1 consist of 2RPIR Muruks from Moem, Goldie Warriors, defending Champions, Igam 1134 Crocs and the Long Range Reconnaissance Unit Troopers.

Tournament hosts, the Headquarter Chiefs are drawn in Pool 2, against tournament favorites, Basilisk Marlins, 1RPIR Diggers from Taurama, Air Transports Wing Eagles and the Force Support Battalion Tigers.

In the opening match today, the Basilisk Marlins edge out hosts Headquarter Chiefs 18-13 while the second match saw the Long Range Reconnaissance Unit Troopers up against the Lombrum Sharks.

A try from the Sharks, forced a 5-all draw at half time, however a penalty in the second half put the Green Shadows up on a good start to the tournament with a win.

Day 2 of the tournament is scheduled for Monday the 21st September.

item.title: Court orders State to pay K52. 2 million compensation for Madang town land
item.description: A long- running Human Rights court case by landowners of the land on which Madang town sits, against the State; has finally come to a close after the National Court in Madang ruled that the plaintiffs, who are the ten landowner clans, be compensated justly. The landowners took the matter to court for breach of their rights and were seeking Protection from Unjust Deprivation of Property under Secti
item.content:encoded:
A long- running Human Rights court case by landowners of the land on which Madang town sits, against the State; has finally come to a close after the National Court in Madang ruled that the plaintiffs, who are the ten landowner clans, be compensated justly.

The landowners took the matter to court for breach of their rights and were seeking Protection from Unjust Deprivation of Property under Section 53 of the Constitution, and Claims for Compensation under Section 53 (2) of the Constitution after establishing liability of the State.

Justice Dr Vergil Narokobi, orderd on September 11, 2026, that the State pays them K52, 200, 000.00 as just compensation for the 1, 280. 52 hectares of land referred to as 'Jomba Plain,' and which includes Modilon- Jomba, Wagol and Wagol Reserve.

The ten clans are Nob, Matulon, Laupain Bilia, Kakon, Asuapain, Mahoban, Uribu, Ga Gali, Bau Malehu, and Kanurua.

The court also ordered that the State pays each of the plaintiffs K5, 220, 000.00 over a 5-year period.

As part of the just compensation on just terms, the court also recommended that pursuant to sub section 25 (3), 53 (2), 57 (5), 155 (4), and 158 (2) of the Constitution to the National Parliament that it exercises its legislative power under section 109 (1) of the Constitution to enact a legislation in similar terms to the Motu- Koita Assembly Act 2007 for the welfare of the indigenous people of Madang, within 12 months from the date of ruling.

Justice Narokobi further ordered that the State pays the plaintiffs interests on the judgement sum at 2% from the date of entry of liability to the date of judgement.

The plaintiffs are the landowners of present Madang Town, and their interest was first recognised by a pre- Independence court between 1971 and 1972.

It was also recognised by the National Land Titles Commission.

The Court heard that in 1988, the then Minister for Lands declared certain areas of Madang Town to be State Land, according to his powers under Section 9 of the National Land Registration Act, 1977.

The plaintiffs were, however; not aware of the notice.

The State, over the years; has been willing to pay compensation but, for some reason, has not done so.

They have proven in a separate case on liability that the areas of land accommodating Madang Township were not properly acquired by the State ( Kusup v Sipison (2023) N10269), and that the State had failed to exercise its duty to properly convert the said land to State Land under the National Lands Registration Act 1977.

Justice Narokobi said the ownership status of these tracts of land was determined by the pre- independence case of Custodian of Expropriated Property v Commissioner of Native Affairs (Re Jomba Plain) [1971- 72] PNGLR 501 ( a case decided in 1932, thereafter also variously referred to as the " the 1932 decision").

The question before the court was how it should assess just compensation after finding that the State has unjustly deprived them of their property under s53 (2) of the Constitution.

Lawyer representing the landowners and plaintiffs, Bradley Baffinu Wak, Principal Lawyer of Bradley & Company Lawyer, welcomed the ruling and humbly requests and invites the Madang MP, Bryan Kramer, and Madang Governor, Ramsey Pariwa to look into this matter seriously and propose a legislation similar to the Motu- Koita Assembly Act of 2007 to satisfy and comply with the court orders.

Mr Wak described Justice Narokobi's ruling a landmark judgement for the Madang Town landowners, adding that their interests must be implemented at all costs.

item.title: Key law and order reforms proposed for Hela
item.description: Hela Governor Philip Undialu has called on the people of Hela to rally behind four sweeping law-and-order reforms announced at the official launch of the Make Hela Safe Again – Gun Surrender Program yesterday in Tari Town. He said these are necessary steps towards finding lasting solutions to tribal fighting, retaliation and destruction in the province.
item.content:encoded:
Hela Governor Philip Undialu has called on the people of Hela to rally behind four sweeping law-and-order reforms announced at the official launch of the Make Hela Safe Again – Gun Surrender Program yesterday in Tari Town.

He said these are necessary steps towards finding lasting solutions to tribal fighting, retaliation and destruction in the province.

Governor Undialu proposed a stronger provincial mechanism chaired by the Provincial Administrator Ronny Angu and deputised by the Provincial Police Commander (PPC), with key sectors represented.

"Subject to enabling legislation, the committee would coordinate responses to tribal fighting, strengthen early-warning systems, protect essential services and infrastructure, and coordinate responses in declared fighting or high-risk zones," he said.

He said people who organise, finance, command or participate in serious violence must no longer be glorified by the term “warlord.” Where there is lawful basis and sufficient evidence, they must be investigated, arrested where legally justified, charged and prosecuted as criminals.

"No individual should be above the law because of their influence, reputation or clan position," he said.

Governor Undialu proposes increasing compensation for a proven killing to K100,000 plus 100 huge-life pigs, subject to legislation and due process.

"The practice of token compensation must end. Most importantly, the burden must not automatically be shifted to an opposing clan. Whoever is legally found responsible must carry responsibility for the loss. Compensation must also never be used as a substitute for criminal justice," he said.

Governor Undialu elaborated that tribal fighting destroys homes, businesses, trade stores, vehicles, machinery, gardens, livestock and other assets worth hundreds of thousands or millions of kina.

He said these losses must be independently assessed and valued. The proposed system would recognise lives lost, injuries and property destroyed or lost.

"Where a legally liable party fails to meet a final compensation order, land and other assets could, where authorised by law, be independently valued and used through lawful enforcement mechanisms to meet the obligation.

“Hela cannot continue doing the same thing and expect a different result. We must be prepared to change the way we deal with killing, fighting and destruction and compensation practices.

“Traditional reconciliation remains important, but it must work alongside the law and must not replace criminal justice,” Governor Undialu said.

The Governor is calling on traditional leaders, churches, women, youths, landowners, victims, government agencies and all people of Hela to rally behind these reforms and work together to Make Hela Safe Again.

item.title: World Bank and UYEP to visit urban youths in Alotau
item.description: A high-level delegation from the World Bank and Urban Youth Employment Project two (UYEP II) will visit Alotau, Milne Bay Province, from tomorrow (20.09.26), to explore skills development, employment, and economic opportunities for youths in the Alotau District. ‎The four-day visit is themed "From Skills to Employment: Connecting Alotau youths with Infrastructure, skills development and Local Econ
item.content:encoded:
A high-level delegation from the World Bank and Urban Youth Employment Project two (UYEP II) will visit Alotau, Milne Bay Province, from tomorrow (20.09.26), to explore skills development, employment, and economic opportunities for youths in the Alotau District.

‎The four-day visit is themed "From Skills to Employment: Connecting Alotau youths with Infrastructure, skills development and Local Economic Opportunities",

‎The high-level consultation will bring together the World Bank, UYEP II, Alotau District and its stakeholders to assess the district's priorities, implementation readiness and opportunities for the proposed Urban Youth Employment Program under phase three (III).

‎The mission will include practical field visits to potential urban work sites, technical and vocational schools, training institutions and local employers.

‎The World Bank team will be led by Elaine Chee, assisted by four other officers, while the team from the UYEP II will be led by the Project Coordination Manager, Tom Gilis, accompanied by one other officer.

The consultation is expected to provide more employment opportunities for youths while strengthening the connection between urban infrastructure improvement, vocational training, local employment and private-sector participation.

‎The Urban Youth Employment Project is a World Bank- backed initiative in PNG designed to help disadvantaged and unemployed young people.
